kept.title: Use of Prototype Pollution susceptible object assignment
kept.description: The `assign` function at src/scimPatch.ts:437 iterates over arbitrary user-controlled property keys and directly assigns them to the target object. Because there is no validation of the key names, an attacker can pass '__proto__', 'constructor', or 'prototype' to manipulate the object's prototype.
steps_to_exploit: Craft a malicious SCIM PATCH operation where the 'value' object contains a key named '__proto__'.
Inject a payload such as 'polluted': 'yes' into the '__proto__' key.
Submit the patch request to the application.
The global object structure is modified, potentially leading to Remote Code Execution (RCE) or Denial of Service (DoS).
kept.impact: Remote code execution or complete application compromise via prototype pollution.

kept.title: Use of Prototype Pollution Gadget
kept.description: The `assign` function uses a recursive path traversal and object property assignment based on untrusted user input without sanitizing keys, leading to potential Prototype Pollution.
steps_to_exploit: Craft a PATCH operation with a nested object property path like 'constructor.prototype.polluted'.
Send the malicious JSON to the scimPatch endpoint.
Observe that the base Object prototype is modified, affecting subsequent object instances.
kept.impact: Can lead to Remote Code Execution, Denial of Service, or bypass of security logic across the entire application runtime.

kept.title: Prototype Pollution via recursive object assignment
kept.description: The `assign` function (src/scimPatch.ts:437) does not sanitize input keys, allowing an attacker to set arbitrary properties on object prototypes (e.g., `__proto__`, `constructor`) when processing patch values.
steps_to_exploit: Craft a SCIM Patch request with an 'add' operation
Set the value to an object containing malicious keys
Observe that the application's global object prototype is now modified
kept.impact: Remote Code Execution (RCE) or Denial of Service by modifying the behavior of built-in objects.
